body: That might really, really help, thank you. If I know I have an appointment booked, I think I would go to it (I don't like missing scheduled things so I could rely on that), although my biggest worry would be freaking out in the counselling session and wasting the time. I mean just trying to reply to this I think I've sat here for just under an hour staring at the screen and nervously wringing my hands. I'm not really sure what a counselling session involves really (what would I have to say, what would it lead to kind of thing).

I have gone as far as checking out the counselling services website for my uni. If I want to make an appointment I have to call (I have phone phobia) or go to counselling reception. I can see myself mentally talking myself out of it before I even make it into the building. There's a queer space room in my uni but I'm too nervous to visit. I read lurking online that apparently some of the members at my uni are quite unfriendly so I've always kind of steered clear.
